To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prime minister and cabinet have been the subject of little academic research; the executive has been the subject of some research; and that the senior public service has been the subject almost exclusively of historical research.

there are no studies of the Australian prime minister and the prime ministership, and that there are no systematic studies of cabinet and cabinet government, and that there is a lack of studies of the role of ministers and their departments.
there is a lack of research into the executive and that the research is not of high quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exercise of power at the centre, and the institutions, processes and conventions through which power is exercised.
the prime minister and his or her office, the role of cabinet and cabinet ministers, the role of the public service, and the role of departments.
the study of the institutions, processes and people that make up the centre of Australian national government, and the study of the ways in which power is exercised at this centre.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the centre of government is not a topic for political science research in Australia.

, with a few exceptions, political science has not been interested in the centre of government and that the centre has not been interested, or at least has not been able, to attract the attention of the academic profession.
the study of the executive is not well developed in Australia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a lack of research on the centre of government in Australia.
there is a dearth of research on the executive and the centre of government in Australia.
the study of the Australian federal system has not been the study of power, or at the least the study of power as it is exercised by and through the institutions of central government.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of the centre of government is a neglected area.
there is much to do in the area of power at the centre.
there is much to be done, and that it will be a major contribution to Australian political science.
